healthInsurance.title: Health insurance
healthInsurance.heroSubtitle: Protect yourself and your loved ones with health insurance. Find the perfect plan for your needs.
healthInsurance.coverageBenefit: ENJOY COMPREHENSIVE HEALTH INSURANCE COVERAGE FOR YOUR PEACE OF MIND
healthInsurance.allAboutHealthInsuranceContent: When you live in Switzerland, you are required to take out health insurance. It covers part of your healthcare costs. How does LAMal work? How much does it cost? Do I also need supplementary health insurance? What are the specifics of health coverage for cross-border workers? Discover everything you need to know about health insurance in Switzerland.
healthInsurance.whatToKnow: Health insurance in Switzerland: what you need to know
healthInsurance.whatToKnowContent: In 1996, a federal law made enrolment in LAMal compulsory. In other words, anyone living in Switzerland is required to take out this health insurance.
healthInsurance.howItWorks: How does health insurance work in Switzerland?
healthInsurance.howItWorksContent: The goal of Swiss health insurance is to guarantee access to basic healthcare in the event of illness, maternity or accident. But it is neither centralised nor managed by the government. It is the Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH) that oversees how private insurers administer health coverage as part of their business.
healthInsurance.basicInsurancePoint1: Covers the policyholder's main healthcare needs
healthInsurance.basicInsurancePoint2: Guarantees at least hospitalisation costs in a shared room
healthInsurance.basicInsurancePoint3: Dental costs and alternative medicine, among others, are not covered by basic compulsory health insurance
healthInsurance.chooseInsurer: You are free to choose the insurer with which you take out a health insurance contract. All family members must be insured, including children.
healthInsurance.newResidents: New Swiss residents have 3 months to choose their health insurer. After this deadline, the cantonal administration automatically assigns them a provider.
healthInsurance.premiumsVary: Health insurance premiums for 2024 vary depending on:
healthInsurance.costFactor5: The selected benefits (for example, accident coverage)
healthInsurance.sameReimbursement: Whatever these factors, the level of reimbursement is the same for everyone.
healthInsurance.subsidies: It is, however, possible to receive reductions on compulsory health insurance premiums, called subsidies. This assistance, paid by the canton, can cover all or part of the premiums.
healthInsurance.howToGet: How do you get compulsory health insurance?
healthInsurance.freeToChoose: All insured persons are free to choose the provider with which they wish to take out a health insurance contract. The insurer has no right to refuse an application. Nor is it permitted to ask a prospective policyholder to complete a health questionnaire when signing the contract.
healthInsurance.compareFactors: Since each insurer can set the premium it wants, it's important to compare several proposals, taking into account:
healthInsurance.compareFactor1: The budget available for compulsory health insurance
healthInsurance.compareFactor4: The policyholder's age and family situation
healthInsurance.supplementaryContent: In addition to basic Swiss health insurance, it is advisable to take out supplementary health insurance.
healthInsurance.whySupplementary: Why take out supplementary health insurance?
healthInsurance.supplementaryReason: Basic health insurance covers only a modest proportion of healthcare costs. As a result, it is recommended to supplement your coverage with a supplementary health contract.
healthInsurance.notMandatory: Unlike basic health insurance, supplementary health insurance is not compulsory.
healthInsurance.lcaInfo: Everything you need to know about the Insurance Contract Act (LCA)
healthInsurance.crossBorderFocus: A closer look at cross-border workers' health insurance
healthInsurance.crossBorderContent: Switzerland is home to a large number of cross-border workers. This is why two schemes have been put in place to provide health coverage for cross-border workers.
healthInsurance.canCrossBorderGetLamal: Can a cross-border worker benefit from LAMal?
healthInsurance.crossBorderOptions: Cross-border workers, whether they live in France and work in Switzerland or vice versa, are required to take out health insurance. They can choose between two options:
healthInsurance.cmu: The CMU (based on the French health insurance system)
healthInsurance.lamalFrontalier: Cross-border LAMal (based on the Swiss system)
healthInsurance.lamalOrCmu: LAMal or CMU? How to choose?
healthInsurance.lamalOrCmuContent: Under the cross-border LAMal scheme, insured persons can receive care in both France and Switzerland. This is not the case with the cross-border CMU, which covers treatment in Switzerland only under certain conditions.
healthInsurance.allHealthFundsContent: With the widest choice of health insurance offers, compare 2024 premiums for basic and supplementary insurance from more than 30 companies in just a few clicks.
healthInsurance.comparisonCriteria: Comparing health insurance: which criteria to use?
healthInsurance.reimbursementDesc: The first thing to watch for when reading a health insurance policy.
healthInsurance.customerServiceDesc: The quality of support provided and policyholders' reviews.

carInsurance.title: Car insurance
carInsurance.heroSubtitle: Protect yourself and your loved ones with car insurance. Find the perfect plan for your needs.
carInsurance.coverageBenefit: ENJOY COMPREHENSIVE CAR INSURANCE COVERAGE FOR YOUR PEACE OF MIND
carInsurance.introContent1: In Switzerland, mobility is an essential part of daily life. With nearly 6 million vehicles on our roads, the need for car insurance becomes obvious.
carInsurance.introContent2: Indeed, whether you own a car, a motorbike or even a scooter, taking out car insurance is not only a legal obligation but, above all, an essential precaution to protect your financial interests and ensure your safety as well as that of other road users.
carInsurance.introContent3: With our Optimis car insurance guide, we'll guide you through the intricacies of this complex system, explaining the different types of coverage available and their crucial importance in protecting your assets and your peace of mind.
carInsurance.basicCoverageIntro: When you take out car insurance in Switzerland, you can choose between several types of coverage, each offering a different level of protection. The three main basic coverages are third-party liability, partial casco and full casco.
carInsurance.civilLiabilityDesc: is the minimum compulsory coverage for all motor vehicles in Switzerland. It covers material and bodily damage that you could cause to third parties in an accident for which you are found liable. However, it does not cover damage to your own vehicle.
carInsurance.partialCascoDesc: is an optional coverage that provides additional protection in the event of claims such as theft, natural events, glass breakage, fire, collisions with animals, marten bites and vandalism.
carInsurance.fullCascoDesc: is the most extensive coverage you can take out. It includes all the guarantees of partial casco, but also adds protection against damage you could cause to your own vehicle in an accident for which you are liable. This coverage is particularly recommended for new or high-value vehicles.
carInsurance.basicCoverageConclusion: I generally recommend carefully assessing your needs and budget before choosing the coverage that suits you best. Third-party liability is essential, but partial and full casco provide additional protection that can prove valuable if something unexpected happens on the road.
carInsurance.complementaryIntro: In addition to the basic coverages, there is a whole range of supplementary guarantees that can be added to your car insurance policy in Switzerland.
carInsurance.passengerInsuranceDesc: This guarantee covers injuries sustained by drivers and passengers in an accident.
carInsurance.parkingDamageDesc: This coverage protects your vehicle against damage caused by unknown third parties while your vehicle is parked.
carInsurance.extendedGlassDesc: This option extends coverage to include damage to headlights, glass parts and similar items.
carInsurance.mobilityAssistanceDesc: This coverage provides assistance in the event of a breakdown on the road.
carInsurance.lossOfUseDesc: This guarantee provides a replacement vehicle if your vehicle is off the road after an accident.
carInsurance.grossNegligenceDesc: This option provides protection against claims or reductions in benefits in the event of gross negligence by the insured driver.
carInsurance.increasedValueDesc: This guarantee ensures compensation higher than the vehicle's current market value in the event of theft or total loss.
carInsurance.bonusProtectionDesc: This guarantee helps avoid an increase in the insurance premium after a claim by maintaining your current bonus level.
carInsurance.franchiseContent1: The deductible (franchise) is an essential element of any car insurance policy in Switzerland. It represents the portion of costs that the policyholder must pay in the event of a claim before the insurer begins to pay compensation.
carInsurance.franchiseContent2: A higher deductible leads to a lower insurance premium, while a lower deductible results in a higher insurance premium. It is therefore a trade-off between the amount you are willing to pay in the event of a claim and the cost of your insurance premium.
carInsurance.franchiseContent3: It is important to note that each type of coverage may have its own deductible. It is therefore crucial to understand the details of your insurance policy.
carInsurance.bonusMalusContent1: In Switzerland, the bonus-malus system is a mechanism used by insurance companies to assess the risk associated with each driver and adjust the car insurance premium accordingly.
carInsurance.bonusMalusContent2: This system is based on a simple principle: drivers who have no accidents or claims are rewarded with a premium reduction, while those who have accidents see their premium increase.
carInsurance.bonusMalusContent3: The bonus-malus system works on levels, where each driver is assigned to a certain level based on their driving history.
carInsurance.bonusMalusContent4: We advise driving carefully and obeying the rules of the road in order to maintain a good driving history and benefit from substantial premium reductions.

homeInsurance.title: Home contents insurance
homeInsurance.heroSubtitle: Protect your home and belongings with home contents & liability insurance tailored to your needs.
homeInsurance.compareDescription: Compare the best home contents insurance on the market.
homeInsurance.protectYourHome: PROTECT YOUR HOME AND BELONGINGS WITH TAILORED INSURANCE
homeInsurance.watchVideo: Discover home contents insurance in video
homeInsurance.videoDescription: Our expert explains everything you need to know about home contents & liability insurance in Switzerland.
homeInsurance.whatIsRcMenageContent: Home contents & liability insurance is the perfect ally to protect both your home and your finances when something goes wrong.
homeInsurance.rcPrivateDesc: covers you if you cause damage to someone else or their property. Imagine your dog bites a passer-by or your child accidentally breaks the neighbour's bike: that's when liability insurance steps in to avoid financial trouble.
homeInsurance.menageDesc: protects everything in your home: furniture, personal belongings, etc. In the event of fire, theft or flooding, this insurance is there for you.
homeInsurance.combinedExplanation: When you combine these two insurances, you get home contents & liability insurance. Many companies in Switzerland offer this dual package, which covers you both for the damage you might cause and to protect your own belongings.
homeInsurance.whatIsCoveredIntro: Wondering what home contents & liability insurance is for in Switzerland? In short, it's the best friend of your home and your wallet! Here's what it usually covers:
homeInsurance.coverFireDesc: No panic if lightning strikes or a fire breaks out.
homeInsurance.coverTheftDesc: Whether it's a burglary, a break-in or even a robbery with violence outside.
homeInsurance.coverNaturalDesc: Floods, storms, avalanches, landslides… The lot!
homeInsurance.coverWaterDesc: Leaking water pipes, faulty washing machines, cracked aquariums, etc.
homeInsurance.coverGlassDesc: Windows, glass furniture, sanitary fittings… It's covered!
homeInsurance.rcCoversSummary: On top of all that, home contents & liability insurance covers your private liability if you cause bodily or material damage to others. In short: your belongings inside your home and your personal liability are protected.
homeInsurance.mandatoryContent1: In Switzerland, private liability insurance (RC) can be mandatory in certain cases, especially if you are a tenant. Landlords like peace of mind and often ask their tenants to provide proof of liability insurance.
homeInsurance.mandatoryContent2: For tenants, private liability insurance therefore becomes almost mandatory at the landlord's request. In other cases it isn't compulsory, but it is strongly recommended to protect you if you cause damage to others.
homeInsurance.mandatoryCantons: Home contents insurance is mandatory in certain cantons such as Vaud and Nidwalden for fire and natural-disaster cover. In these cantons, you must take out a policy with the cantonal fire insurance company.
homeInsurance.combinedInsurance: 4/ Liability + home contents insurance = combine them together!
homeInsurance.combinedIntro: Opting for combined private liability and home contents insurance is the ideal way to simplify your life and protect your home. Here's why:
homeInsurance.benefit1Desc: Taking out two insurances in one is fast and efficient.
homeInsurance.benefit2Desc: No more endless admin — everything is combined in a single contract.
homeInsurance.benefit3Desc: You're covered from A to Z with a combined policy.
homeInsurance.benefit4Desc: You often get a discount by choosing a combined offer.
homeInsurance.benefit5Desc: Add or remove coverage options according to your needs.
homeInsurance.benefit6Desc: The insurance protects all family members.
homeInsurance.howMuchDoesItCost: 5/ Liability + home contents — at what price?
homeInsurance.costContent: Prices vary depending on the insurer, the chosen coverage and the value of the belongings to insure. Compare offers to find the best value for money.
homeInsurance.howToTerminate: 6/ How do you terminate an existing liability & home contents contract?
homeInsurance.terminateContent: Want to terminate your home contents & liability insurance in Switzerland? No worries, here's what you need to know! To terminate, you'll need a few details:
homeInsurance.terminateInfo4: A reason for termination (nothing very detailed)
homeInsurance.terminateDeadline: Then send your termination letter respecting the notice period, which varies from 1 to 3 months before the end of your contract. If you forget, your contract will be automatically renewed for another year.
homeInsurance.optimisHelps: 7/ Want to save? Optimis helps you!
homeInsurance.optimisHelpsContent: Want to save or improve your coverage? Optimis helps you with these steps transparently and free of charge. Compare offers and find the best home contents & liability insurance for you!

legalProtection.title: Legal protection
legalProtection.heroSubtitle: Protect yourself against disputes and legal costs with tailored legal protection insurance.
legalProtection.legalDefenseDesc: In the event of a dispute
legalProtection.compareDescription: Compare the best legal protection insurance on the market.
legalProtection.protectYourRights: PROTECT YOUR RIGHTS WITH LEGAL PROTECTION INSURANCE
legalProtection.videoDescription: Our expert explains everything you need to know about legal protection insurance in Switzerland.
legalProtection.whatIsLegalProtection: What is legal protection insurance in Switzerland?
legalProtection.whatIsLegalProtectionContent: As a resident in Switzerland, you could face various disputes throughout your life. For example, you might buy a faulty product in a shop and be met with a refusal to refund.
legalProtection.whatIsLegalProtectionContent2: Legal protection insurance can prove to be a lifeline in such situations. By covering all the costs associated with legal proceedings, it provides essential peace of mind.
legalProtection.whatIsLegalProtectionContent3: Whether you initiate the legal proceedings or you are being sued, this insurance protects you by covering the costs generated by the dispute.
legalProtection.typesOfProtection: What are the different types of legal protection?
legalProtection.typesContent: Legal protection insurance offers extensive coverage for different types of disputes:
legalProtection.typeCirculationDesc: protects you in the event of a road-traffic dispute, whether you are a driver, passenger or vehicle owner.
legalProtection.typeEnterpriseDesc: covers you in the event of a dispute related to your professional activity, with a client, an employee or over equipment-purchase matters.
legalProtection.typePrivateDesc: concerns disputes under private law: consumer matters, employment, matrimonial law, neighbourhood, tenancy, etc.
legalProtection.typesNote: Good to know: For private and traffic legal protection, you can opt for individual or family cover.
legalProtection.coveredItem1: Legal costs, such as lawyer's fees
legalProtection.coveredItem2: Legal advice to guide you through your steps
legalProtection.coveredItem3: Support from a professional during proceedings
legalProtection.coveredItem5: Advance of criminal bail to avoid imprisonment
legalProtection.coveredItem6: The opposing party's procedural costs if you lose
legalProtection.coveredItem7: Free choice of your lawyer for the legal proceedings
legalProtection.notCoveredItem1: Disputes against your own legal protection insurer
legalProtection.notCoveredItem2: Coverage exclusions for intentionally committed offences
legalProtection.guaranteesNote: Good to know: Your contract may include coverage exclusions. Before subscribing, make sure to carefully check these exclusions and any waiting period.
legalProtection.prices: How much does legal protection insurance cost?
legalProtection.pricesContent: Premiums generally range between CHF 150 and 400 per year depending on the extent of coverage and the options chosen. Compare offers to find the best value for money.
legalProtection.whyNeedIt: Why should you have legal protection insurance?
legalProtection.whyReason1: With legal protection insurance, you make significant savings. The costs related to a dispute can quickly add up. All lawyer's fees are covered.
legalProtection.whyReason2: More efficient dispute management: with legal protection, you benefit from advice and support from professionals.
legalProtection.waitingPeriodNote: Please note: the waiting period is generally 3 months, and legal protection will not cover you for disputes that occurred beforehand.
legalProtection.terminationContract: Commitment and termination of a contract
legalProtection.terminationContent: The ability to terminate legal protection insurance depends on the insurer and the specific terms of each contract. As a rule, contracts are annual and renew automatically.
legalProtection.terminationContent2: To terminate, you generally need to respect a 3-month notice period before the contract's expiry date. Termination must be done by registered letter.
legalProtection.top10Tips: Optimis's top 10 tips for choosing your legal protection
legalProtection.tip1: Research the different insurers using comparators.
legalProtection.tip2: Carefully check the guarantees and exclusions of each contract.
legalProtection.tip3: Examine the insurer's reputation and financial strength.
legalProtection.tip4: Carefully compare the rates of legal protection insurance.
legalProtection.tip5: Favour contracts offering free choice of lawyers.
legalProtection.tip6: Check whether you don't already have legal protection in another contract.
legalProtection.tip7: Take into account the waiting periods and termination terms.
legalProtection.tip8: Make sure that the specific disputes that concern you are included.
legalProtection.tip9: Ask people around you for recommendations or check online reviews.
legalProtection.tip10: Precisely determine the type of contract you need.
legalProtection.coverageTypesContent: Legal protection covers different areas of law to protect you day to day.
legalProtection.whyNeedItContent: Legal costs can quickly reach thousands of francs. Legal protection lets you assert your rights without financial worry.
legalProtection.howToChooseContent: Compare offers according to your specific needs and personal situation.
legalProtection.costsContent: Premiums vary depending on the extent of coverage and your profile. Compare to find the best value for money.

lifeInsurance.heroSubtitle: Prepare for your retirement and save on taxes with tailored life insurance.
lifeInsurance.protectYourFuture: PREPARE FOR YOUR FUTURE AND SAVE ON YOUR TAXES
lifeInsurance.feature4: Up to CHF 7,056 in deductible taxes
lifeInsurance.videoDescription: Our expert explains everything you need to know about life insurance and the third pillar (3a) in Switzerland.
lifeInsurance.whatIsLifeInsuranceContent: Life insurance in Switzerland is a financial product that combines savings and protection. It lets you build up capital for your retirement while protecting your loved ones in the event of death or disability.
lifeInsurance.typesContent: There are different types of life insurance in Switzerland:
lifeInsurance.type1: Pure-risk life insurance: protection in the event of death only
lifeInsurance.type2: Mixed life insurance: a combination of savings and protection
lifeInsurance.type3: Fund-linked life insurance: savings invested in funds
lifeInsurance.thirdPillarContent: The third pillar is a private pension system in Switzerland. It complements the 1st and 2nd pillars (AVS and LPP) to ensure a comfortable standard of living in retirement.
lifeInsurance.pillar3aDesc: Pillar 3a (tied): tax-deductible, capped amount, limited withdrawals
lifeInsurance.pillar3bDesc: Pillar 3b (flexible): no tax deduction, no contribution limit, free withdrawal
lifeInsurance.whoNeedsItContent: Life insurance is particularly recommended for:
lifeInsurance.needCase4: Anyone wishing to optimise their taxes
lifeInsurance.howToChoose: How to choose your life insurance?
lifeInsurance.howToChooseContent: To choose the right life insurance, assess your protection and savings needs, compare the returns offered and check the surrender conditions.
lifeInsurance.taxBenefitsContent: Contributions to pillar 3a are fully deductible from your taxable income, up to the annual ceiling.
lifeInsurance.maxDeduction: Up to CHF 7,056 in deductions per year
lifeInsurance.maxDeductionDesc: For employees affiliated with a pension fund (2024)

becomeOwner.subtitle: The complete step-by-step guide
becomeOwner.intro: Buying a home in Switzerland rests on 3 pillars: enough equity, an affordable financial burden and the right mortgage. We explain each step, then connect you free of charge with the best financing and pillar 3a offers.
becomeOwner.s1Body: Banks apply two golden rules. Your theoretical costs (interest calculated at a prudent rate of around 5%, amortisation and maintenance) must not exceed one third of your gross income. In parallel, you must provide at least 20% of the purchase price in equity.
becomeOwner.s1Point2: Maintenance estimated at 1% of the property value
becomeOwner.s1Point3: The mortgage covers at most 80% of the price
becomeOwner.s2Body: Of the required 20% equity, at least 10% must come from «hard» funds (savings, pillar 3a, gift) — excluding the 2nd pillar. The remaining 10% can be topped up with your occupational pension assets.
becomeOwner.s2Point2: Savings, pillar 3a, gift or advance inheritance
becomeOwner.s3Body: Home ownership promotion (EPL) lets you use your pension for your primary residence: early withdrawal (you take out the capital) or pledging (you pledge without withdrawing, to keep the tax advantage). A well-built pillar 3a greatly accelerates the build-up of your equity.
becomeOwner.s3Point1: Early withdrawal or pledging of the 2nd pillar
becomeOwner.s3Point2: Withdrawal of pillar 3a for the down payment
becomeOwner.s3Point3: Open a 3a now to save and reduce your taxes
becomeOwner.s4Body: Fixed rate for security, SARON for flexibility: the right choice depends on your horizon and risk tolerance. Comparing several lenders can save tens of thousands of francs over the term.
becomeOwner.s4Point1: Fixed rate (2 to 15 years): guaranteed payments
becomeOwner.s4Point3: Compare banks and insurers for the best rate
becomeOwner.crossTitle: The 2 levers to finance your purchase
becomeOwner.mortgageCardDesc: Compare fixed and SARON rates from several lenders for free and get the best financing offer.
becomeOwner.pillarCardDesc: Build your equity while reducing your taxes. Compare the best pillar 3a solutions.
becomeOwner.faq1Q: How much equity do you need to buy in Switzerland?
becomeOwner.faq1A: At least 20% of the purchase price, of which at least 10% in «hard» equity (savings or pillar 3a), excluding the 2nd pillar. For an 800,000 CHF property, that's 160,000 CHF, of which 80,000 CHF excluding LPP.
becomeOwner.faq2Q: Can I use my 2nd pillar to become a homeowner?
becomeOwner.faq2A: Yes, through home ownership promotion (EPL): you can withdraw (early withdrawal) or pledge your LPP assets to finance your primary residence.
becomeOwner.faq3Q: What financial burden can I bear?
becomeOwner.faq3A: Your theoretical costs (interest at the ~5% calculation rate, amortisation and maintenance) must not exceed one third of your gross income. This is the first calculation the bank makes.
becomeOwner.ctaTitle: Ready to make your project happen?
becomeOwner.ctaDesc: Compare the best financing and pillar 3a offers in Switzerland for free. No commitment.

privacyPolicy.title: Privacy policy
privacyPolicy.introContent: OptimisLink Sàrl is the owner of the optimis.ch website and acts as the controller of personal data within the meaning of the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP). We have drawn up this privacy policy to set out our approach to processing the information collected through our website. It is essential that you read it before using our online services. Protecting your personal data is an absolute priority for us, and we are committed to ensuring its confidentiality and security. All data is hosted in Switzerland with the company Infomaniak Network SA.
privacyPolicy.dataCollectionContent: When you visit our site, certain information about your device is automatically collected, such as your web browser, your IP address, your time zone and the cookies installed on your device. In addition, we record information about the pages or products you view, the websites or search terms that referred you to our site, and your interactions with our site. This automatically collected information is referred to as "device information". Furthermore, we may collect personal data that you choose to provide to us (such as your surname, first name, address, payment information, etc.) when you register or use certain features of the site.
privacyPolicy.dataUsageTitle: For what purpose do we process your data?
privacyPolicy.dataUsageContent: We only process the personal data necessary for the proper functioning of the site and the security of our users' data. The automatically collected information is used to detect potential abuse and compile site usage statistics, without allowing individual users to be identified. You can visit our site without revealing your identity or providing personal data. However, if you wish to use certain features or receive our newsletter, you will need to provide us with personal data. If you choose not to provide it, some features of the site may not be accessible.
privacyPolicy.rightsContent: In accordance with the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP), you have certain rights regarding your personal data, including the right of access, rectification, deletion and portability of your data. You may also object to the processing of your data or request that its processing be restricted. To exercise these rights, please contact us using the details provided below.
privacyPolicy.dataSharingContent: When you request a comparison, a quote or advice, you consent to the data you provide to us (surname, first name, contact details and information relating to your request) being transmitted to one or more partner insurance brokers, independent and registered in the FINMA register of insurance intermediaries, so that they can contact you and draw up an offer suited to your situation. This transmission is based solely on your consent, which you can withdraw at any time by writing to us at contact@optimis.ch. Without consent, we are unable to process your connection request. Our partners act as independent data controllers for the data transmitted to them and are required to comply with the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP). We do not sell or rent your data for advertising purposes.
privacyPolicy.contactContent: For any questions regarding this privacy policy or your rights concerning personal data, please do not hesitate to contact us by email at contact@optimis.ch.

about.title: About Optimis
about.missionContent: Optimis was founded with a clear mission: to simplify insurance comparison in Switzerland and help individuals and businesses find the best offers suited to their needs. We believe everyone deserves easy access to optimal protection at the best price.
about.valuesContent: Independence, transparency and customer service are at the heart of our approach. We are not tied to any insurer, which allows us to offer objective and impartial comparisons. Our team is committed to supporting you at every step of your insurance search.
about.historyContent: Since our founding, we have helped thousands of Swiss residents save on their insurance. Our platform compares offers from more than 30 partner insurance companies, covering every type of insurance: health, car, home contents, legal protection, life and much more.
about.teamContent: Our team of insurance experts is based in French-speaking Switzerland. We combine in-depth knowledge of the Swiss insurance market with cutting-edge technology to offer you the best possible service.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Find answers to the most common questions about our services and insurance in Switzerland.
faq.q1: How does the Optimis comparator work?
faq.a1: Our comparator analyzes offers from more than 30 partner insurers to present the best options for your profile. Simply fill in the form, and we'll instantly show you the offers best suited to your needs.
faq.a2: Yes, our comparison service is 100% free and with no commitment. We are paid by insurers when you take out a policy through our platform, which allows us to offer you this service free of charge.
faq.q3: Can I change my health insurance at any time?
faq.a3: Basic insurance (LAMal) can be cancelled each year by 30 November, effective 1 January. Supplementary insurance policies have their own cancellation terms, usually with 3 months' notice.
faq.q4: How are health insurance premiums calculated?
faq.a4: Premiums depend on several factors: your canton of residence, your age, the insurance model chosen (standard, family doctor, HMO, telemedicine) and the amount of your deductible.
faq.q5: What is the health insurance subsidy?
faq.a5: The subsidy is financial support paid by the cantons to help people on modest incomes pay their health insurance premiums. Eligibility conditions vary from canton to canton.
faq.q6: What is the difference between partial and full casco?
faq.a6: Partial casco covers damage caused by third parties, theft, natural events and glass breakage. Full casco additionally covers damage you cause to your own vehicle.
faq.q7: How long does it take to receive a quote?
faq.a7: Our comparisons are instant. As soon as you've filled in the form, you immediately receive the offers matching your profile.
faq.a8: Absolutely. We comply with Swiss data protection law. Your information is encrypted and never shared without your explicit consent.

professionalInsurancePage.heroSubtitle: Professional liability, LAA, LPP, Legal protection – Compare the best offers for your business in Switzerland.
professionalInsurancePage.typesSubtitle: Discover the essential cover to protect your business, your employees and your professional assets.

rcPro.title: Professional liability
rcPro.desc: Professional liability insurance covers damage caused to third parties in the course of your business. It is mandatory for many professions in Switzerland.
rcPro.details: This insurance covers the bodily, material and financial damage you could unintentionally cause to a client or third party. The level of cover varies according to your sector. Regulated professions (doctors, lawyers, architects, trustees) are required by law to hold professional liability insurance.

laa.title: Accident insurance (LAA)
laa.desc: LAA accident insurance is mandatory for every employer in Switzerland. It covers your employees' occupational and non-occupational accidents.
laa.details: LAA covers medical costs, daily allowances in the event of incapacity to work and invalidity pensions. Employees working more than 8 hours a week are covered for both occupational AND non-occupational accidents. Self-employed people can take out LAA voluntarily.

lpp.title: Occupational pension LPP (pillar 2)
lpp.desc: The LPP occupational pension is mandatory from an annual salary of CHF 22,050. It ensures your employees maintain their standard of living in retirement.
lpp.details: Pillar 2 complements the AVS (pillar 1) and is an essential part of retirement provision in Switzerland. As an employer, you must affiliate your employees with a pension institution. Contributions are shared between the employer (at least 50%) and the employee. Comparing offers helps you find the best terms and returns.

legalProtection.title: Professional legal protection
legalProtection.desc: Professional legal protection defends you in disputes related to your business: contracts, employment law, commercial leases, etc.
legalProtection.details: This insurance covers lawyers' fees, court costs and expert assessments in the event of a dispute. It covers contractual disputes with your clients or suppliers, conflicts with employees (employment law), tax litigation and disputes relating to your commercial premises.

lossOfEarnings.title: Sickness loss-of-earnings insurance
lossOfEarnings.desc: Sickness loss-of-earnings insurance guarantees the payment of salary in the event of incapacity to work due to illness, for you or your employees.
lossOfEarnings.details: Without this insurance, the employer is required to pay the salary according to the Bern or Basel scale (from 3 weeks to 6 months depending on seniority). Loss-of-earnings insurance takes over and generally pays 80% of the salary for 720 days. It's a key factor in attracting and retaining talent.

multiRisk.title: Business all-risk insurance
multiRisk.desc: All-risk insurance protects your premises, equipment, stock and business against unforeseen damage (fire, water damage, theft, etc.).
multiRisk.details: This comprehensive cover includes commercial buildings, professional furniture and equipment, stock and goods, as well as business interruption in the event of a claim. It allows you to quickly resume your business after an unexpected event.

cyber.title: Cyber insurance
cyber.desc: Cyber insurance protects your business against digital risks: hacking, ransomware, data breaches, service interruption.
cyber.details: With growing digitalization, cyberattacks represent a major risk for Swiss SMEs. This insurance covers data restoration costs, crisis management, notifications to affected individuals (GDPR/FADP), third-party damage and business interruption caused by a cyberattack.

professionalInsurancePage.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about business insurance

faq.q1: Which insurances are mandatory for a business in Switzerland?
faq.a1: Mandatory insurance depends on your status and sector: LAA (accidents) is mandatory for every employer, LPP (pension) from an annual salary of CHF 22,050, and professional liability is required for certain regulated professions (doctors, lawyers, architects, etc.).
faq.q2: Does a self-employed person need the same insurance as an Sàrl?
faq.a2: No. A self-employed person with no employees is not subject to the same obligations. They can take out LAA and LPP voluntarily. However, as soon as they employ staff, the obligations are the same as for an Sàrl or SA.
faq.q3: How much does business insurance cost in Switzerland?
faq.a3: Costs vary considerably depending on the sector, the size of the business and the cover chosen. Professional liability can cost from CHF 300 to 5,000/year, LAA represents 0.5% to 3% of payroll, and LPP between 7% and 18% of the coordinated salary.
faq.q4: How do I choose the right provider for my business insurance?
faq.a4: Compare offers from several insurers taking into account price, extent of cover, deductibles and customer service. Use our comparator to receive free, personalized offers tailored to your situation.

lpp.faq1Answer: Vested benefits is an account to which your LPP assets (pillar 2) are transferred when you leave a job in Switzerland without immediately starting another.
lpp.faq2Answer: It applies to every change of job, move abroad, transition to self-employment or period of unemployment.
